stages.name: Persistence via Tasks and Run Keys

scenario.summary: Threat actors use SEO poisoning and malvertising to lure users to fake verification pages (ClickFix) that trick them into executing malicious PowerShell commands from their clipboard. These commands download multi-stage payloads that establish persistence through scheduled tasks and Run keys, eventually deploying DLL sideloading chains for reverse SSH tunnels or Node.js-based RATs.

meta.rationale: The hunt begins by identifying the most likely targets—hosts with web browsers or Node.js—using software inventory, then searches for DNS and execution telemetry specifically on those hosts.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has lured users to a malicious site that tricks them into pasting a PowerShell command from the clipboard, which then executes and stages a malicious payload.

hunt.name: ClickFix Redirection and Script Execution
hunt.description: ClickFix represents a refined social engineering attack where malicious sites mimic legitimate verification checks or document tools. This hunt identifies the initial access vector by finding DNS requests to known lure domains and corroborates these with rare PowerShell executions involving clipboard operations and file staging evidence. An agent evaluates the chain of redirection and execution to identify successful social engineering completions.

nodes.label: Scope to hosts with web browsers or Node.js

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%chrome%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%edge%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%firefox%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%safari%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%node.js%')
config.description: Identify hosts that possess the primary attack surface (web browsers) or specific runtimes (Node.js) mentioned in the ClickFix campaigns.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts currently running software that facilitates the ClickFix lure or payload execution.

primitive_config.label: Scope to hosts with web browsers or Node.js
primitive_config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%chrome%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%edge%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%firefox%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%safari%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%node.js%')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts currently running software that facilitates the ClickFix lure or payload execution.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{lure_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify hosts that visited the malicious redirection domains.
config.expected_signal: Hosts resolving known malvertising or typosquatted domains associated with the ClickFix campaign.

primitive_config.label: DNS lookups to lure domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{lure_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Hosts resolving known malvertising or typosquatted domains associated with the ClickFix campaign.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS executions, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%get-clipboard%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%6341434163416441%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY cmd HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Detect PowerShell commands that interact with the clipboard or use specific hex strings found in ClickFix payloads, stack-counting to isolate rare behaviors.
config.expected_signal: Highly specific PowerShell commands used to retrieve and execute code from the user's clipboard. Typical administrator use of Get-Clipboard is expected to be more common than attacker scripts.

primitive_config.label: Rare PowerShell clipboard operations
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS executions, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe') AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%get-clipboard%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%6341434163416441%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY cmd HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
primitive_config.expected: Highly specific PowerShell commands used to retrieve and execute code from the user's clipboard. Typical administrator use of Get-Clipboard is expected to be more common than attacker scripts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\cf_verify.zip' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\\6341434163416441.txt') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Search for specific files created by ClickFix PowerShell stagers in temporary directories.
config.expected_signal: Creation of a ZIP archive or a temporary text file containing encoded PowerShell in directories like ProgramData or Temp.

config.objective: Determine if any host resolved a lure domain and shortly after executed a PowerShell command retrieving data from the clipboard, specifically looking for those that also created the mentioned staging files.

config.expected_signal: A high-confidence verdict for hosts showing the full redirection-to-execution chain.

config.description: Confirm the agent's findings and identify any follow-on activity such as DLL sideloading or persistence.
config.instructions: 1. Review the rows cited by the triage agent. 2. Verify the browser history or DNS logs on the affected host for visits to the lure domains. 3. Check for the existence of the C:\ProgramData\ staging directories mentioned in the report. 4. If confirmed, pivot to investigating DLL sideloading (CertEnroll.dll) or reverse SSH tunnels (r.ps1).
